item.title: The Return of the Alien Tort Statute
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch outlines how the Alien Tort Statute is reemerging as a major legal issue, with a pending Supreme Court case potentially providing guidance to plaintiffs and companies on what torts are covered and who can be considered a defendant.

item.description: Matt Mande and Gregory C. Allen provide a detailed overview Maven Smart System, the AI-powered software platform that has enabled a revolution in military targeting.

item.title: Why the West Keeps Losing Critical Mineral Assets to China
item.description: China is winning the race for critical minerals long before mines enter production. As Chinese firms acquire strategic mineral assets worldwide, the United States and its allies need new tools to identify, protect, and compete for ownership of future supply.

item.description: The United States has stepped up economic, political, and military pressure on Cuba. This commentary examines five possible scenarios involving the use of force against Cuba.

item.title: No Time to Ease In: Immediate Priorities for Frank Garcia, the State Department’s New Africa Lead
item.description: After more than a year without a Senate-confirmed leader at the State Department’s Africa Bureau, Frank Garcia takes office at a pivotal moment for U.S.-Africa policy.

item.title: Economic Modernization and Strategic Positioning of Algeria
item.description: As Algeria opens up and diversifies its economy, it will have to navigate complex relationships with major powers and neighbors, create meaningful employment for its youth, and sustain economic reforms.

item.description: At a macro level, President Xi is likely hoping to demonstrate a dynamic leading role on the international stage—particularly within the China, Russia, Iran, North Korea (CRINK) grouping of revisionist autocracies—while portraying U.S. influence globally as in decline.

item.title: Reengaging the Solomon Islands: A Strategic Opportunity for the United States
item.description: Matthew Wale’s rise to power offers Washington its best opportunity in years to rebuild ties with the Solomon Islands, but seizing the moment will require more than diplomatic rhetoric.

item.title: Strategic Clarity: Reassessing the Value of China to Korea
item.description: As Xi visits North Korea, South Korea should reassess its China strategy, recognizing a shift from complementarity to competition and Beijing’s unhelpful role on North Korea, and pursue strategic clarity based on a strong U.S.-ROK alliance and trilateral ties with Japan.

item.title: Banning Gasoline Exports Will Harm U.S. Energy Security
item.description: As the world borrows from oil inventory “savings” to offset the Middle East Gulf export closure, U.S. gasoline prices are likely to rise. But policymakers should avoid bad ideas like banning exports, which are prone to backfiring by ultimately raising prices and undermining energy security.

item.description: Aalok Mehta and Lauryn Williams unpack the Trump administration’s new executive order on cybersecurity risks from AI, arguing that its light-touch approach fails to adequately address mounting public concern over a lack of AI regulation.

item.description: The United States and its allies face a growing threat from an axis led by China and Russia. This report outlines a two-war planning construct focused on Asia and Europe, and a wartime industrial base focused on low-cost unmanned systems and long-range precision strike.
